name: TextBox 4
text: Priority selection searches the worst availability regions first

name: TextBox 6
text: Rank events by the worst availability during their interval.Search the worst priority level first, expand only if needed.Move one check, then rebuild later events using A/B/C/D rules.Update incrementally by removing old intervals and add the rebuilt intervals and score once.Deterministic, rule-compliant, and substantially faster.Measured result: min 15→18, std 1.96→1.44.

name: TextBox 14
text: Try the worst group first.20 checks × 2 shifts = 40 proposals.Take the best improvement in that group.Expand only if it finds none.

name: TextBox 4
text: Simulated Annealing with Variable Neighbourhood Search

name: TextBox 7
text: Prioritise checks on the worst daysRebuild later checks after a moveUpdate availability incrementallyKeep only improving schedules

name: TextBox 10
text: Use the same variable neighbourhoodsExplore feasible changes to the scheduleAlways accept an improving scheduleSometimes accept a worse schedule at high temperatureCool down and return the best-so-far schedule

name: TextBox 12
text: Simulated Annealing adds temperature-based acceptance to the existing neighbourhood search

name: TextBox 28
text: Temperature can accept a worse schedule, including a lower worst day. These moves become rarer as the search cools.

name: TextBox 30
text: Reject every move that lowers worst-day availability. Anneal only when the worst day is unchanged.

name: TextBox 32
text: Always return the best-so-far schedule. Temporary deterioration never replaces the best result.

name: TextBox 34
text: Same input and half-step neighbourhoods. Compare tuned Priority Based Selection with VNS against Simulated Annealing, using the median of seeds 1–3. Keep only if all seeds retain 18 aircraft, smoothness improves by at least 0.005, and median runtime stays within 300 seconds.

name: TextBox 9
text: Same priority-based selection neighbour search algorithm

name: TextBox 11
text: Better moves are always kept. Worse moves can still be kept early on, by chance.

name: TextBox 13
text: Over time we accept fewer worse moves, so the search settles on a strong plan.

name: TextBox 16
text: Think of the search like walking over hills. Today’s method only walks uphill. That is fast and safe, but you can get stuck on a steep part of the hill when a better peak is nearby.Simulated annealing sometimes takes a downhill step early, so you can leave a trap and reach a better overall schedule. As the search “cools,” those downhill steps become rare, and we settle on the best plan we found.

name: TextBox 6
text: Rank checks by the worst day they cover.Search the worst priority group first.Move one check, then rebuild the later checks on that aircraft.Remove old intervals and add rebuilt intervals to availability.Verify maintenance rules and non-overlap.
